citations.title: On the (Ir)Replaceability of Global Setups, or How (Not) to Use a Global Ledger
citations.finding: Prints NO ledger functionality -- a composition-theory paper whose running example is the box above. Establishes that realizing G_ledger does not license using it as a global setup: 'the UC security of Bitcoin for realizing a ledger proved by Badertscher et al. [CRYPTO'17] is not sufficient per se to allow us to replace the ledger by Bitcoin when used as a global setup.' Its concrete counterexample against this box is adversarial reordering (a simulator exploiting it has nothing to exploit once the ledger is replaced by a blockchain that orders partly by honest miners); its general rule is that 'an extensive adversarial interface at the global setup hinders its replacement'. Positive characterizations in Theorems 3.3, 3.5 and 3.10. This is where the stub title's word 'irreplaceability' comes from, and the claim checks out.
